subject: raw data organisation for multiple memory cards of a single camera ID

messages.author: eaef3f939fe23a83
messages.subject: raw data organisation for multiple memory cards of a single camera ID
parts:
Dear all,
I´d like to start using the camtrapR workflow but I do have a question concerning the directory structure (i.e. the raw camera trap data organisation) and I did not find relevant information so far.

I do have data from camera traps that operated from spring to autumn without changing their location. During this period the camtraps have been checked several times - including memory card replacements.
In some cases we needed to adjust the internal time of the camera because it was not specified correctly (or malfunction in some rare cases). After adjustment the internal time was (obviously) correct. Therefore only a subset of the images of a camera need adjustment of the time shift.
According to the vignette it is only possible to shift the time of the whole directory of a camera (or a station).
Therefore I´d ask you for any ideas on raw data organisation in such cases. 

As a workaround, my idea is to rename the ID of the camera for each memory card replacement using the same coordinates (a combination of camera ID and memory card replacement). Are there any reasons against this approach?

Thanks in advance!

Best regards
Frederik

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: raw data organisation for multiple memory cards of a single camera ID
parts:
Hi Frederik,
I'll need some more information to answer you properly. When you replaced memory cards, did you keep those images in separate subfolders for each replacement. If so, would all images in those memory card directories need to be renamed, or also only some? And do you have a study design with one or multiple cameras per station?

If it is one camera per station and all images in a specific memory card directory need to be renamed, it should be possible to trick the function and make it consider the memory card directory a "camera". That would also require giving that "camera" ID in the time shift table. 
All other cases would be more complicated. If that's the case please let me know and we'll see about that. 
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.author: eaef3f939fe23a83
messages.subject: Re: raw data organisation for multiple memory cards of a single camera ID
parts:
Hi Jürgen,
thanks a lot for your answer! 
Concerning your questions: Yes, I do keep those images in separate subdirectories and all images within certain directories need to be corrected (time shift).
Currently I only do have one camera per station where the problem occurred but I will go for 2 cameras per station in the future. So for now your suggestion should do the trick but a general solution would be preferable. I think I´m going to write a custom R-script to correct the time (at the basis of each replaced memory card) before the camtrapR workflow and afterwards move (or better symlink) the images into a proper directory hierarchy to proceed with camtrapR. I am happy to share the code in case you´re interested.

Best regards
Frederik

parts:
Hi Frederik,
I believe it should be rather straightforward to add support for an additional folder in timeShiftImages. That would mean you would need an extra column in the time shift table too. 
If you come up with a solution, please feel free to share the code for other users. If more people need this functionality I might then also add it to an upcoming release, but so far haven't done any work on it and won't have much time in the near future. 
Cheers,
Jürgen
